title: Optimize walkthrough — Fidelity Lane stress test (INT8 vs FP8)
summary: Redwood AE + SE demo of the Optimize console focusing on Fidelity Lane (INT8 vs FP8) profiles. Walkthrough included latency/quality tradeoff charts, sample prompt regressions, and a short stress test showing tail latency under bursty traffic. Customer flagged requirements around SSO, KMS, and a desire for a small pilot on Dedicated capacity. Agreed next steps: send qprofile CSV, pilot pricing, and run a 48-hour benchmark with NimbleRetail prompts under Redwood Dedicated trial nodes.
topics: Why Fidelity Lane vs Cost Lane
INT8 artifacts and expected quality delta
KV cache reuse and prefix caching
action_items: Jordan Patel - Share Optimize qprofile CSV and sample console export - due 2025-09-03
Maya Lin - Spin up quick Dedicated trial config and provide runbook for NimbleRetail - due 2025-09-05
Aisha Gomez - Send top 50 customer-facing prompts for regression tests - due 2025-09-02

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-29 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel; Maya Lin; Samir Khosla; Aisha Gomez; Ben Carter; Priya Rao; Liam O'Neill

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'll kick us off, we also have Maya on the call who'll do the optimize walkthrough and a quick stress test, Samir is on for product questions.
[00:18] Aisha: thanks Jordan, excited to see the fidelity lane stuff — we've been wrestling with INT8 artifacts in prod.
[00:27] Maya: awesome, we'll show the console flows; quick agenda: 1) high-level qprofile concepts, 2) console demo switching between lanes, 3) latency/quality charts and an on-the-fly stress run, 4) security/ops notes.
[00:45] Ben: quick ask — we'll be testing inside our VPC, any special steps for Dedicated?
[00:53] Jordan: yes, Dedicated supports VPC peering and private endpoints; Maya will show the Dedicated profile later, but key point is you can pin a profile per-model or per-route.
[01:10] Maya: opening the Optimize tab in the Console... you can see our qprofiles grouped into Cost Lane / Balanced / Fidelity Lane. I'm clicking into Fidelity Lane for the Llama-2-70b variant we onboarded.
[01:34] Maya: the fidelity lane increases fp8 usage and relaxes some per-layer quant clamps; it's intended to reduce quant-induced hallucinations compared to aggressive int8.
[01:50] Priya: sorry, can i interrupt — you said fp8, is that hardware-dependent? We run mixed GPU fleet.
[01:58] Maya: good q — fp8 benefits are most consistent on latest gen GPUs (e.g., H100/A100 with fp8 kernel support). On older hardware we emulate fp8 which is slower. That's why we show expected latency deltas in the profile.
[02:15] Liam: show us the expected token latency vs quality chart.
[02:22] Maya: switching to the chart view... here are two curves: INT8 profile (orange) and FP8 Fidelity Lane (blue). On median latency INT8 is ~25% faster, but for some prompt classes the quality drop is visible — we surface BLEU-like and ROUGE proxies and a custom regression score.
[02:46] Maya: i'll run a quick A/B with a sample prompt from NimbleRetail (Aisha shared earlier). Queueing both profiles on the same request pattern.
[03:05] [03:05] Speaker 2: (background) oh sorry — wrong mic.
[03:12] Maya: okay the console supports side-by-side compare, you can see tokens produced, per-token time, and a diff view that highlights hallucinations and missing entities. Note the int8 output truncates one of the SKU IDs in this sample, that's the kind of regression we'd flag.
[03:40] Aisha: that's exactly the issue we've seen with INT8 in checkout flows — SKU mismatch. How often do you see that?
[03:48] Maya: depends on distribution; in our logs for similar e-comm workloads INT8 had a ~3.4% regression on entity fidelity versus fp8's ~0.6% under the same prompt set. Those numbers are workload dependent — we recommend running your top 50 prompts.
[04:10] Ben: what's the KV cache interaction — will caching reduce the delta?
[04:18] Maya: yes, prefix caching often mitigates repeated context losses. If you have stable system prompts or repeated conversation prefixes, the effective difference shrinks because the cache avoids re-quantizing many tokens.
[04:33] Jordan: i'm going to switch to stress scenario — we'll execute a 10-minute burst with mixed short/long prompts to show tail latency. Maya, you can start the runner?
[04:41] Maya: starting now — running 200 req/s for a 10 minute burst on a small Dedicated config.
[05:05] [05:05] (console updates)
[05:18] Maya: early results: median latency for INT8 was 12ms per token, fp8 ~15ms per token; tail p95 for INT8 spiked to 320ms under a cache miss pattern, fp8 p95 stayed around 220ms. So INT8 had slightly faster steady-state but worse tail in this run.
[05:48] Priya: that tail spike is concerning, is it due to kernel fallbacks?
[05:55] Maya: likely yes — when a model hits certain sequence lengths or internal kv eviction we fall back to slower execution or memory copies. The runtime tries to batch and avoid that, but INT8's tighter memory footprint can cause fragmentation in some cases leading to fallback costs.
[06:16] Aisha: is there an automated suggestion? We saw Optimize propose a hybrid profile earlier in the UI.
[06:25] Maya: exactly — Optimize's suggestion engine can recommend a hybrid setting: run FP8 on the first N tokens (system + prompt) then INT8 for the rest, or pin FP8 for routes flagged as high-fidelity. That typically gets you most of the cost benefit while reducing the high-severity regressions.
[06:46] Liam: curious about cost math — show us a ballpark per-token cost delta.
[06:52] Maya: in this config FP8 net cost was ~1.4x INT8 per token in cloud pricing, but because INT8 sometimes causes re-tries or post-processing checks at the application layer, effective product cost can be higher. We have a token-level cost breakdown in Console and you can simulate traffic to estimate monthly $$ impact.
[07:15] Ben: any flags for on-prem HSM/KMS usage?
[07:20] Jordan: we support KMS integration for Private deployments and Dedicated can be configured with customer-managed keys; Maya will share the security docs. We are SOC2 Type II compliant and have an ISO journey in progress.
[07:38] Aisha: can you run the test with our actual prompts? We want to see SKU hallucinations specifically.
[07:44] Maya: that's the plan for the 48-hour benchmark pilot — we ask you to upload the top prompts and a small labeled ground truth set. We'll run INT8/FP8/hybrid and produce a regression report.
[08:00] [08:00] (15 minute demo segment skipped for brevity in notes)
[23:05] Maya: picking back up — here's a per-prompt regression heatmap. Prompts with long product lists show the most delta. The console flags tokens that differ from ground truth and assigns severity.
[23:34] Priya: can we export that csv? we'll ingest into our own monitoring.
[23:40] Maya: yes, exportable CSV and a JSON API. Link: https://console.redwood.ai/exports/pilot-2025-nimbleretail
[24:02] Aisha: how are rollouts handled? we want gradual traffic shifting.
[24:09] Samir: rollouts are route-based — you can configure a canary percent or A/B experiment and Redwood will route requests according to traffic weights. There's an automatic fallback policy if quality regressions exceed thresholds.
[24:30] Ben: latency SLOs — how do you measure and alert?
[24:36] Maya: built-in tracing, token-level latency histograms, and integration with PagerDuty/Slack. You set SLOs per-route and Optimize will recommend cache/batch tweaks if you're missing targets.
[24:55] Liam: any gotchas with batching + fp8?
[25:01] Maya: batching often dominates efficiency, but fp8 kernels can be more sensitive to batch size; smaller batches sometimes negate the fp8 advantage. Optimize simulates batching distributions from your traffic traces to recommend batch sizes.
[25:23] Aisha: security: SAML + user provisioning — we must map RBAC to teams.
[25:30] Jordan: supported — SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, granular RBAC for route/model access.
[25:40] Priya: can we see the audit logs? we need raw call logs for compliance.
[25:45] Jordan: audit logs retained per your retention policy; for Private you can push logs into your own SIEM.
[25:56] [26:00] Jordan: quick demo pivot — live edit of a qprofile. Maya, change the fp8 intensity from aggressive to conservative.
[26:07] Maya: editing... changing per-layer clamp, toggling hybrid mode, save and deploy to canary. Deployed — route now sends 5% traffic to new profile.
[26:25] Ben: can you rollback automatically on regressions?
[26:29] Maya: yes you can set automatic rollback thresholds (e.g., >1% regression on entity fidelity) and the system will revert.
[26:40] Aisha: about benchmarks — we run encrypted PII in prompts, is there support for redaction?
[26:48] Jordan: we recommend client-side redaction for PII in many cases; Redwood supports redact-at-ingest and also has options to opt out of data logging for routes. Dedicated/Private gives more control.
[27:02] Maya: switching to a quick network view — CPU/GPU utilization during the burst. Notice INT8 run shows slightly higher GPU utilization but larger memory churn leading to p95 spikes.
[27:19] Priya: what's fragmentation mitigation? can we pre-warm KV caches?
[27:24] Maya: yes pre-warming and pinning certain prefixes helps; also the runtime can reserve reserved segments to reduce fragmentation. We'll include recommended params in the runbook.
[27:38] Aisha: team question — how long to get Dedicated up?
[27:43] Jordan: typical lead time for a small Dedicated pool is 2-4 weeks for enterprise onboarding; trial nodes can be available faster depending on capacity. Maya will scope a trial node offering for NimbleRetail.
[28:00] Liam: cost vs commit?
[28:03] Jordan: we offer reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits; pilot pricing will be time-limited. We'll include both on-demand and a reserved quote.
[28:18] Maya: ok let's run the final comparison table — INT8, FP8, Hybrid. Column: median latency, p95 latency, entity fidelity regression, cost multiplier. Populating...
[28:33] Maya: INT8: median 12ms, p95 320ms, fidelity regression 3.4%, cost 1.0x. FP8: median 15ms, p95 220ms, fidelity regress 0.6%, cost 1.4x. Hybrid: median 13ms, p95 210ms, fidelity regress 1.0%, cost 1.15x. (numbers illustrative, will be run against your prompts).
[29:05] Aisha: those hybrid numbers look interesting.
[29:10] Maya: Optimize can generate that table from your actual traffic and show cost vs quality curves. We can attach a CSV with simulated monthly spend given your token estimates.
[29:22] Ben: any mention of licensing or model variants? we use an internally fine-tuned Llama-2-70b.
[29:29] Jordan: supported — you can bring custom model weights to Dedicated/Private; we provide a model onboarding checklist. Samir, note to send onboarding doc link.
[29:42] Samir: noted.
[29:48] Aisha: time to talk about SLA — we need an uptime commitment and latency SLOs.
[29:54] Jordan: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; for Hosted we offer best-effort. We'll surface SLA terms in the commercial proposal.
[30:06] [30:06] Maya: quick Q&A — Priya asked about monitoring integration; we push metrics to Prometheus and have Grafana dashboards out of the box.
[30:22] Priya: good. I'm curious about data residency for EU customers.
[30:27] Jordan: we support region pins and for Private you can host fully on-prem.
[30:33] Liam: ok let's talk logistics for the 48-hour benchmark — scope, success criteria, and data transfer.
[30:41] Jordan: suggested scope: 48 hours, run INT8/FP8/Hybrid on Dedicated trial nodes, ingest top 50 prompts and 250 labeled responses, measure entity fidelity, latency, cost. Success if hybrid reduces cost at <1% fidelity regression vs FP8.
[31:05] Aisha: that success criteria is reasonable. We'll prepare the labeled responses.
[31:12] Ben: any risk of training-data leakage with logs?
[31:17] Jordan: logs are treated as telemetry; for Private/Dedicated you can opt out of persistent logging. We'll include recommended settings for no-logging.
[31:30] Maya: demo wrap up — showing the final compliance slide (SOC2, KMS, SAML) and the security doc link: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 and the pilot runbook: https://redwood.ai/pilot/runs
[31:56] [32:00] Jordan: open floor for any final Qs.
[32:05] Aisha: two quick items — 1) can Redwood run the pilot inside our AWS account (VPC peering preferred) and 2) we want the rollback automation to be tuned to our entity fidelity metric rather than generic score.
[32:18] Maya: yes to both. We'll need an IAM role for peering and we can configure the rollback threshold to use your provided metric.
[32:30] Ben: will the trial Dedicated nodes support our instance types? we mostly use A100s.
[32:36] Jordan: we can provision A100-backed nodes for Dedicated trials, subject to capacity.
[32:42] Liam: timeline check — if we approve the pilot this week, when can you start?
[32:48] Jordan: if we get prompts and sign-off, we can aim to start within 7–10 business days for a small trial. Full Dedicated onboarding is longer.
[32:59] Aisha: ok we'll aim to get materials by next Tue.
[33:05] Maya: i'll note a quick checklist: prompts, labeled responses, desired metrics, IAM for VPC peering.
[33:15] Jordan: wrap recap: Jordan to send pilot pricing + qprofile CSV; Maya to provision trial config and runbook; Aisha to send prompts.
[33:30] [33:30] (brief cross talk)
[33:40] Ben: one more operational question — do you support canary percent schedules (time based) or only percentage routing?
[33:48] Maya: both. You can schedule percent ramps over time or use percentage-based steady routing. We also support traffic shaping by key (e.g., 10% of users).
[34:05] Priya: what's the best way to ingest our labeled ground truth securely?
[34:11] Jordan: S3 presigned uploads into a customer-owned bucket with role-assume works well — we'll include instructions.
[34:23] Aisha: will Redwood sign a DPA?
[34:27] Jordan: yes, standard DPA is available; for enterprise we'll do custom terms.
[34:36] Samir: note to attach the DPA template in the follow-up.
[34:41] Jordan: sure.
[34:45] Maya: final question — do you want us to run a small internal smoke test using just 1k requests first? That can surface config issues quickly.
[34:53] Aisha: yes please do.
[35:00] Maya: we'll run the smoke test and then the 48-hour benchmark.
[35:06] Jordan: ok final logistics — next meeting to review benchmark results, i'll calendar a 1-hour tech sync for two weeks out.
[35:15] Aisha: sounds good.
[35:20] Liam: thanks everyone.
[35:25] Jordan: thanks, bye.
[35:30] [35:30] (recording ends)

Notes on transcript quality: auto transcription introduced occasional speaker mislabels and dropped punctuation; some product names transcribed variably (FP8 shown as F P eight in a few spots).
